questions.question: BPL is an economic benchmark related to threshold income. What does "BPL" stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Below Poverty Line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Below Poverty Line (BPL):-**

 
 
• It is a benchmark used by the government of India** to indicate economic disadvantage and to identify individuals and households in need of government assistance and aid.**
 
• It is determined using various parameters which vary from state to state and within states.
 
• The BPL benchmark is used by the government **to target various social welfare programs and schemes to the poorest and most vulnerable sections of society.**
 
• The BPL concept is also used by various non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and other charitable institutions to identify and target their poverty alleviation and development programs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Base Price Line:-**

 
 
• **It is a pricing strategy that involves setting different prices for products within a product line, based on their perceived value or quality. **
 
• The goal of base price lining is to maximize profits by offering customers a range of choices at different price points, while still maintaining a consistent brand image.
 
 
 
• **Below Price Line:-**
 
 
• **It is a term used to describe products that are priced below the average market price for similar products.**
 
• This can be done for a variety of reasons, such as to attract new customers, to increase sales volume, or to clear out inventory.

questions.question: Which is the smallest planet of our solar system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mercury**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mercury**:-

 
 
• **Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System and the closest to the Sun. (Hence option 3 is correct)**
 
• It is a terrestrial planet, meaning that it is made of rock and metal like Earth.
 
• Mercury has a heavily cratered surface due to overlapping impact events.
 
• These features are well preserved since the planet has no geological activity and an extremely tenuous atmosphere called an exosphere.
 
• Despite being the smallest planet in the Solar System with a mean diameter of 4,880 km (3,030 mi), 38% of that of Earth, Mercury is dense enough to have roughly the same surface gravity as Mars.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earth**:-

 
 
• **It is the third planet from the Sun and the only known planet in the universe to support life. **
 
• It has a liquid water ocean, a nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere, and a solid surface.
 
• Earth is also home to a diverse range of plants and animals.
 
 
 
• **Mars**:-
 
 
• **It is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second smallest planet in the solar system. **
 
• It is a rocky planet with a thin atmosphere and a cold, dry surface. Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos.
 
 
 
• **Venus**:-
 
 
• **It is the second planet from the Sun and the hottest planet in the solar system. **
 
• It has a thick atmosphere that is mostly carbon dioxide and a surface that is hot enough to melt lead. Venus has no moons.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the harvest festivals celebrated in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Diwali:-**

 
 
• **Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights.**
 
• It is one of the most important and popular festivals in India, and is also celebrated by Hindus around the world.
 
• **Diwali symbolizes the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance.**
 
• Diwali is celebrated on the darkest night of the Hindu lunar month Kartika, which typically falls between mid-October and mid-November in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The festival lasts for five days, and each day has its own special significance.
 
• **It is not a harvest festival celebrated.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Baisakhi festival

 
 
• **Baisakhi is a major event for the farmers as it commemorates the harvest time of the Rabi season.**
 
• Wheat crops could be seen growing and swinging all across Punjab at this time of year.
 
• Sikhs hold kirtans, visit local Gurdwaras, and community fairs, hold Nagar kirtan processions, raise the Nishan Sahib flag, and gather to socialize and share festive foods.
 
 
 
• Lohri:
 
 
• Lohri, the bonfire harvest festival of Punjab celebrated in the month of Magh, is symbolic of new beginnings.
 
• The festival is celebrated every year on January 13 with much enthusiasm and zeal.
 
• This festival denotes the harvesting of the Rabi crops and hence all the farmers get together in order to thank god for giving them such a wonderful harvest.
 
• The rituals related to Lohri symbolize the attachment of the people with Mother Nature.
 
 
 
• Onam:
 
 
• **It is a harvest festival of Kerala.**
 
• It is celebrated to commemorate the arrival of King Mahabali.
 
• The festival lasts for ten days.
 
• It is also a harvest festival and falls on the 22nd Nakshatra Thiruvonam in the Malayalam calendar month of Chingam, which in the Gregorian calendar overlaps with August–September.

questions.question: In October 2022, who became the first Indian-origin Prime Minister of UK?
questions.solution:
The correct answer __**Rishi Sunak.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rishi Sunak:-**

 
 
• **He became the first Indian-origin Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in October 2022. (Hence option 3 is correct)**
 
• Sunak entered politics in 2015, when he was elected as the Member of Parliament for Richmond (Yorks).
 
• He was appointed Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Local Government in 2018, and then Chief Secretary to the Treasury in 2019.
 
• Sunak is the first British Asian and the first Hindu prime minister of the United Kingdom.
 
• His election is a significant moment for British politics, and it is a testament to the growing diversity of the UK population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kamala Harris:-**

 
 
• **She is an American politician and attorney who is the 49th and current vice president of the United States. **
 
• A member of the Democratic Party, she previously served as the attorney general of California from 2011 to 2017 and as a U.S. senator representing California from 2017 to 2021. 
 
 
 
• **Harry Anand:-**
 
 
• He is an American chemical engineer and politician.
 
• **He served as the mayor of Laurel Hollow from 2007 to 2013. **
 
• He was the first Indian-American mayor in the state of New York.
 
 
 
• **Neel Kashkari:-**
 
 
• **He is the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis. **
 
• He is an American banker, economist, and politician. 
 
• He worked as a management consultant at McKinsey & Company before joining the U.S. Treasury Department in 2006.

questions.question: Which caves are considered as the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India dating back to the Maurya period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barabar and Nagarjuni caves.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barabar and Nagarjuni Caves:-**

 
 
• These are located in the Jehanabad district of the Indian state of Bihar.
 
• **These caves were carved out of granite rocks during the Maurya Empire (322-185 BCE), and some of them have Ashokan inscriptions. (Hence option 3 is correct)**
 
• The caves are known for their high level of architectural and craftsmanship skills.
 
• The Barabar caves are a group of four caves located on the Barabar hill.
 
• These caves were built for the Ajivika sect, a religious group related to Jainism.
 
• The caves are divided into two chambers: a large rectangular hall and a smaller, circular, domed chamber. The large hall was used for worship and ceremonies, while the smaller chamber was used for meditation and spiritual practice.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bagh Caves:-**

 
 
• **These are a group of nine rock-cut monuments, situated among the southern slopes of the Vindhyas in Bagh town of Dhar district in Madhya Pradesh state in central India. **
 
• These monuments are located at a distance of 97 km from Dhar town. 
 
 
 
• **Elephanta Caves:-**
 
 
• **The Elephanta Caves are a collection of cave temples predominantly dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva. **
 
• They are located on Elephanta Island, or Gharapuri (literally meaning "the city of caves"), in Mumbai Harbour, 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) east of Mumbai in the Indian state of Maharashtra. 
 
 
 
• **Ajanta and Ellora Caves:-**
 
 
• These are two of the most important and impressive cave temple complexes in the world.
 
• **They are located in the state of Maharashtra, India, and were carved out of solid rock between the 2nd century BC and the 11th century AD.**

questions.question: Budhaditya Mukherjee is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Budhaditya Mukherjee:-**

 
 
• Pandit Budhadityaji was born in 1955 in Durg, Chattisgarh.
 
• He is considered as the leading sitarist of his generation. (Hence option 4 is correct)
 
• Budhadityaji received his entire training in Sitar from his father, Pandit Bimalendu Mukherjee.
 
• He has, since 1979, performed in 26 countries including the UK., USA., Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the UAE, Armenia, and in almost all European countries.
 
• On June 30, 1990, Budhaditya Mukherjee created history by becoming the first-ever musician to perform at the House of Commons, London.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Veena:- 

 
 
• The veena is a plucked string instrument that is popular in Indian music.
 
• It has a long and rich history, dating back to ancient times.
 
• The veena is mentioned in the Rigveda, one of the oldest Hindu scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Violin:-**
 
 
• The violin is a stringed instrument that is played with a bow.
 
• It is one of the most popular instruments in the world, and it is used in a wide variety of musical genres, including classical, folk, jazz, and rock.
 
 
 
• **Sarangi**:-
 
 
• The sarangi is a bowed string instrument that is popular in Indian music.
 
• It has a long and rich history, dating back to at least the 13th century.
 
• The sarangi is known for its expressive and soulful sound, and it is often used to accompany vocalists or to play solo.

questions.question: Provisions related to the Panchayats are mentioned in which part of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part IX:-**

 
 
• The idea of the Panchayati Raj system in India signifies the system of rural local self-government.
 
• The 73rd Amendment Act added a new part IX and articles 243 to 243 O to the Indian constitution.
 
• The 73rd Amendment act of the Indian constitution gave constitutional status to the Panchayati raj system.
 
• The term Panchayati raj was coined by Jawahar Lal Nehru.
 
• The Panchayati Raj Act came into force on 24th April 1993.
 
• April 24th is observed as the national Panchayati raj day since 2011.
 
 
 
• Important committees constituted for recommendations regarding Panchayati raj in India:
 
 
• Balwant Rai Mehta committee.
 
• V.T. Krishnammachari committee.
 
• Ashok Mehta Committee.
 
• G.V.K. Rao Committee.
 
• L.M. Singhvi Committee.
 
• P.K. Thungon Committee

questions.question: After the Battle of Plassey 1757, who from the British East India Company, became Baron of Plassey?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Clive.**__

__
 
• **Robert Clive:-**

 
 
• He was a British general and statesman who played a key role in the establishment of British rule in India.
 
• He is best known for his victory at the Battle of Plassey in 1757, which gave the British East India Company control of the Bengal Presidency.
 
• **The Baron of Plassey was Robert Clive, 1st Baron Clive of Plassey, (Hence option 1 is correct).**
 
• **Clive served as Governor of Bengal twice, and during his second term he implemented a number of reforms that helped to consolidate British rule.**
 
• He also expanded the British Empire in India by conquering new territories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Warren Hastings:-**

 
 
• **He was the first Governor-General of Bengal and is considered one of the most controversial figures in British colonial history. **
 
• He was a brilliant administrator and diplomat, but he was also accused of corruption and tyranny.
 
 
 
• **John Laird Mair Lawrence:-**
 
 
• He was an English-born Ulsterman who became a prominent British Imperial statesman.
 
• **He served as the Viceroy of India from 1864 to 1869.**
 
 
 
• **Charles James Napier:-**
 
 
• **He was a British general who is best known for his conquest of the Sindh province in India in 1843. **
 
• During his time as Governor, Napier introduced a number of reforms, including:
 
 
• Abolishing slavery.
 
• Reforming the tax system.
 
• Building new roads and irrigation canals.
 
• Establishing a new judicial system.

questions.question: Who among the following succeeded Ghatotkacha, the Gupta ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta I.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Chandragupta I (319AD-334 AD):

 
 
• He was the first Gupta ruler to assume the title of *Maharajadhiraja*.
 
• He strengthened his kingdom by the matrimonial alliance with the powerful family of Lichchhavis, who were the rulers of Mithila.
 
• He got married to the Lichchhavi princess *Kumaradevi*.
 
• He started the Gupta Era in 319AD-320 AD.
 
• He established his authority over Magadha, Saketa and Prayaga.
 
• **Ghatotkacha was succeeded by his son, Chandragupta I.**
 
• Chandragupta was the son of Gupta king Ghatotkacha and the grandson of the dynasty's founder Sri Gupta. He ruled from 319 to 335 CE.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kumaragupta I:-

 
 
• ​He was the son and successor of Chandragupta II.
 
• Kumaragupta I's reign was marked by peace and relative inactivity, which was a result of the stability and prosperity achieved during the reign of his father, Chandragupta II.
 
 
 
• Skandagupta:-
 
 
• Skanda Gupta also took the title Vikramaditya.
 
• Shrigupta was the first Gupta ruler of the Gupta Dynasty.
 
• He took the title of Maharajadhiraja.
 
• Bhitari pillar depicts the information about Skandagupta of the Gupta Empire.
 
 
 
• Chandragupta II:-
 
 
• One of the most powerful emperors of the Gupta dynasty was Chandragupta II, also known by his given name Vikramaditya and Chandragupta Vikramaditya. (Hence option 4 is correct)
 
• He was the third ruler of the Gupta Empire in India.
 
• The famous Chandragupta II was the child of Samudragupta and Datta Devi.
 
• The Gupta empire was extended by Chandragupta II to the western sea coast, a vital area for trade and commerce.

questions.question: Teejan Bai was awarded a Padma Bhushan for her art in 2003. She is a great exponent of which dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandavani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Teejan Bai:-**

 
 
• **She is a renowned Pandavani singer from Chhattisgarh, India.**
 
• Pandavani is a traditional folk art form in which stories from the Mahabharata are narrated with musical accompaniment. 
 
• Teejan Bai is known as the first female exponent of Pandavani. 
 
• Teejan Bai learned Pandavani singing from her maternal grandfather, Brijlal Pardhi, who was a renowned Pandavani artist.
 
• Teejan Bai listened to and memorized Mahabharata stories from her grandfather from a young age.
 
• She started singing Pandavani at the age of 13. She soon impressed people with her talent and won several awards, including the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Ghoomar:-**

 
 
• **It is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, India. **
 
• It is primarily performed by women, who wear a veil and a flowing dress called a ghaghara.
 
• The dance begins with slow movements that gradually become faster, and the dancers' veils flutter in the air. During the dance, the dancers often move their hands and feet in delicate and graceful movements.
 
 
 
• **Kalbelia:-**
 
 
• **It is a folk dance form of the Kalbelia people, a snake-charming tribe from the Thar Desert in Rajasthan, India. **
 
• The dance is an integral part of their culture and performed by men and women.
 
 
 
• **Chhau dance:-**
 
 
• **It is a semi-classical Indian dance form with martial and folk traditions. **
 
• It is found in three styles named after the location where they are performed: the Purulia Chhau of West Bengal, the Seraikella Chhau of Jharkhand, and the Mayurbhanj Chhau of Odisha.

questions.question: Lord William Bentinck with the support of Raja Rammohan Roy abolished the practice of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sati**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sati:-**

 
 
• It is the name of an ancient Indian practice where women would die in the pyre of her dead husband.
 
• The practice was voluntary but most of the time, it was involuntary.
 
• If a woman had no surviving children who could support her, she was pressured to accept sati.
 
• Lord William Bentinck with the support of Raja Rammohan Roy abolished the practice of Sati.
 
• Bentinck passed the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829.
 
 
• He issued Regulation XVII declaring Sati to be illegal and punishable in criminal courts.
 
• The ban was met by uproar because many people supported Sati at the time.
 
• The matter went to the Privy Council in London.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Polyandry**:-

 
 
• It is a form of polygamy in which a woman takes two or more husbands at the same time.
 
• It is contrasted with polygyny, involving one male and two or more females.
 
• Polyandry is a rare form of marriage, but it is practiced in some parts of the world, including the Tibetan Plateau, Nepal, and the Marquesas Islands.

questions.question: Where is the Jawahar Lal Nehru Port located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Navi Mumbai.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawahar Lal Nehru Port :-**

 
 
• It is also known as Nhava Sheva Port.
 
• It is the second busiest container port in India, after Mundra Port.
 
• **It is located on the eastern shores of the Arabian Sea in Navi Mumbai, Raigad district, Maharashtra. (Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• JNPT is operated by the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust Authority (JNPTA). 
 
• **JNPT was commissioned on May 26, 1989, and has since grown to become one of the most important ports in India. **
 
• It handles around 50% of the total containerized cargo volume across the major ports of India.
 
• JNPT is connected to over 200 ports in the world, making it a major hub for international trade.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Port of Kolkata:-**

 
 
• **It is also known as Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, is the only major riverine port in India. **
 
• **It is located on the eastern bank of the Hooghly River, about 203 kilometers (126 miles) from the sea. **
 
• The port is a major hub for the export and import of goods, including coal, iron ore, steel, and agricultural products. 
 
• It was established by the British East India Company in 1775 and played a major role in the development of trade and commerce in India.
 
• The port was also a major center for the freedom struggle during the British colonial period.
 
 
 
• Port of Chennai:-
 
 
• **It is also known as Kamarajar Port.**
 
• It is the second busiest port in India, after Mundra Port.
 
• **It is located on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal, in the city of Chennai, Tamil Nadu. **
 
• The port is a major hub for the export and import of goods, including automobiles, electronics, textiles, and agricultural products.

questions.concept: Ecology and Functions of an ecosystem
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a terrestrial ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grasslands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Terrestrial Ecosystem:-**

 
 
• It is an ecosystem that is found on land, as opposed to an aquatic ecosystem, which is found in water.
 
• Terrestrial ecosystems are characterized by their dominant vegetation of trees, shrubs, grasses, and other land plants.
 
• They also include a wide range of animals, from insects and birds to mammals and reptiles.
 
• The type of terrestrial ecosystem found in a particular place is dependent on the climate, soil, and topography of that area.
 
• **Grasslands are an example of a terrestrial ecosystem.**
 
 
 
• **Grasslands:-**
 
 
• These are characterized by their dominant vegetation of grasses and herbaceous plants, with few or no trees.
 
• They are found in all parts of the world, and cover about 20% of the Earth's land surface. 
 
• Grasslands are important ecosystems for a variety of reasons.
 
• They provide food and habitat for a wide range of animals, including both herbivores and carnivores. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ocean:-**

 
 
• It is a continuous body of salt water that is contained in an enormous basin on Earth's surface.
 
• The major oceans and their marginal seas cover nearly 71 percent of Earth's surface, with an average depth of 3,688 metres (12,100 feet).
 
 
 
• **River:-**
 
 
• It is a natural flowing watercourse, usually a freshwater stream, flowing on the surface or inside caves towards another waterbody at a lower elevation, such as an ocean, sea, bay, lake, wetland, or another river. 
 
 
 
• **Pond:-**
 
 
• It is a small, still body of water that is typically smaller and shallower than a lake.
 
• Ponds can be natural or artificial, and they are found all over the world.

questions.question: Which of the following options does NOT constitute a national income measurement method?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit method.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Credit method:-**

 
 
• **The credit method is a way of avoiding or reducing double taxation. **
 
• It works by allowing taxpayers to credit the taxes they have paid in one country against the taxes they owe in another country.
 
• This is especially important for taxpayers who live or work in multiple countries, or who receive income from multiple countries.
 
• **The credit method does not constitute a national income measurement method.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Product method:**

 
 
• This method measures the total value of all final goods and services produced in a country during a given period of time.
 
• It is also known as the value-added method.
 
 
 
• **Income method**:
 
 
• This method measures the total income earned by all factors of production (land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship) in a country during a given period of time.
 
 
 
• **Expenditure method:**
 
 
• This method measures the total expenditure on final goods and services produced in a country during a given period of time.

questions.question: The Zo-Mal-Lok folk dance is associated with which community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Lepcha community.**__

__
 
• **Zo-Mal-Lok:-**

 
 
• **It is a folk dance is associated with the Lepcha community of Sikkim and Darjeeling. **
 
• It is a group dance that is performed to celebrate the agricultural cycle of paddy cultivation.
 
• The dance is performed by both men and women, who wear traditional Lepcha costumes and dance to the accompaniment of traditional Lepcha musical instruments such as the tungbuk (bamboo flute), yangjey (stringed instrument), cymbal, and drum.
 
 
 
• **Lepcha community:-**
 
 
• This community is an indigenous people of the Himalayan region, with a population of around 11,000.
 
• They are found primarily in the state of Sikkim in India, as well as in neighboring parts of Bhutan, Nepal, and West Bengal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jamatia community:-**

 
 
• **It is one of the 19 indigenous tribes of Tripura, a state in northeastern India. **
 
• They are the third largest tribe in the state, with a population of over 83,000.
 
• The Jamatias are also found in neighboring Bangladesh and Myanmar.
 
 
 
• **Chaimal community:-**
 
 
• **The Chaimal community is a small indigenous tribe of Tripura, a state in northeastern India. **
 
• Their total population is only about 550 people, and they are primarily concentrated in the Ambassa subdivision of the Dhalai district.
 
 
 
• **Lushai community:-**
 
 
• **The Lushai community, also known as the Mizo community, is an indigenous people of Northeast India and neighboring parts of Bangladesh and Myanmar. **
 
• They are the largest ethnic group in the Indian state of Mizoram.

questions.question: With respect to sports, WADA stands for ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Anti-Doping Agency.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** World Anti-Doping Agency:-**

 
 
• **WADA is an international independent organization composed and funded equally by the sport movement and governments of the world. **
 
• It was established in 1999 to promote and coordinate the fight against doping in sport internationally.
 
• WADA's key activities include:
 
 
• **Scientific research**
 
• **Education**
 
• **Development of anti-doping capacities**
 
• **Monitoring of the World Anti-Doping Code (Code) - the document harmonizing anti-doping policies in all sports and all countries**
 
 
 
• WADA also maintains the Prohibited List, which is a list of substances and methods that are prohibited in sport. The Prohibited List is updated annually to reflect the latest scientific and medical knowledge.

questions.question: Vetti tax is the most frequently mentioned tax in the inscription of Cholas who ruled in Tamil Nadu. This tax was taken in the form of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**forced labour.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vetti Tax:-**

 
 
• **It was a form of forced labor tax levied by the Chola dynasty in southern India. (Hence Option 4 is correct)**
 
• It was the most frequently mentioned tax in Chola inscriptions.
 
• Under the Vetti system, common people were forced to work for the king or their village landlords without any wages.
 
• The Vetti tax was used for a variety of purposes, such as construction and maintenance of public works, such as roads, irrigation systems, and temples.
 
• It was also used to support the military and the royal court.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other various taxes imposed by the Chola dynasty:-
 
 
• **Land tax (Kadamai):** This was the most important tax, and was levied on all agricultural land. The rate of tax varied depending on the type of crop and the quality of the land.
 
• **House tax (Manaiya):** This was a tax levied on all houses, regardless of their size or value.
 
• **Market tax (Shulka)**: This was a tax levied on all goods bought and sold in markets.
 
• **Professional tax (Pesha):** This was a tax levied on people who practiced certain professions, such as merchants, artisans, and doctors.
